description: The drift guarantee, asserted as behavior: a lib member the baseline states no color for floors. `WeakRef.prototype.deref` is one — the gate cannot construct a `WeakRef` to probe, and an unprobed clean claim ships with its color absent rather than asserted — so `reference.deref()` is reported, and a TypeScript release landing ahead of a `@no-throw/core` release floors its newcomers the same way.

diagnostics.message: Call to `reference.deref` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it is declared without a body — an ambient declaration, a `.d.ts`, or a value known only by its function type — and no mark, manifest, overlay, override or baseline entry colors it, so it is assumed to throw. Your outs, in precedence order: bridge this call with `try`/`catch`; assert the color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@no-throw/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.
